findings.finding: F1: the model plan (LEGSMOKE-1117) pinned line 1 as the title with its (/tmp/…) suffix cut (48 bytes), while every marker of this generation on main carries the full title.
findings.answer: Line 1 pinned to `LEGSMOKE-1124: Upgrade rehearsal fallback child (/tmp/legion-e2e4b.1546829.WGpv3Ou5)` + LF, 85 bytes, sha256 f96cdff6…, blob 1c98eccf…; the Constants table says the 48-byte form is superseded; pre-state fact 5 has the implementer re-read the title with `dispatch read` and every phase recomputes the digests from the literal before quoting them.

findings.finding: F2 (architect-only): the root spec says the pull request changes no other file, yet the branch carries .legion/LEGSMOKE-1124/*.json and the merge may carry one docs/solutions note; the model plan attributed that allowance to the root spec, which does not contain it.
findings.answer: AC4 is written in two halves (branch side: marker + .legion/LEGSMOKE-1124/; merge side at HR and M: marker + zero or one docs/solutions/legion/*-LEGSMOKE-1124.md) and sources the allowance to skill://legion-worker and skill://legion-retro, not the spec. Recorded as specDepartures[0] with kind changed on the substituted Acceptance 2 line, for the architect to decide.

findings.finding: F3: nothing in the model plan said which head carries the green gate the merge needs; the approved head is a trailered handoff head with zero check-runs (BLOCKED).
findings.answer: Constants define HR as retro's untrailered removal commit; AC5 states that BLOCKED + total_count 0 at a trailered head is the expected shape and that gate comes back green at HR (measured on #767's head 4afb9ed7: check ×2, gate ×2, all success); Integration says the merger reads gate at HR.

findings.finding: F4 (architect-only): the second-line trigger 'a review finding that asks, in words' is not machine-decidable, ignores that an APPROVED review ends implementing, and had no cap.
findings.answer: AC3/D4: the trigger is a CHANGES_REQUESTED review on the pull request whose body asks for one more line in smoke/LEGSMOKE-1124.md, read with `gh api pulls/<n>/reviews`; messages and comments do not count; K ≤ 1, a second request goes to the architect. The plan expects the one-line file and does not instruct the reviewer to request line 2; whether this run must exercise the second-line path is named as the architect's call.

findings.finding: F5: the line-2 wording in the draft facts had no source in the repository; main holds a 24-marker convention `Legion proof review round 1 (LEGSMOKE)`.
findings.answer: D3 pins line 2 to the convention; the two-line digests were recomputed from that literal: 124 bytes, sha256 c00a02b6…, blob 83b95d4b….

findings.finding: F6 (architect-only): the child spec is empty; the root's Acceptance names LEGSMOKE-1121 and one file through one merged pull request while the root has three children each landing a marker.
findings.answer: Sources quotes the four substituted lines verbatim with their source; D1 states that no single child satisfies the root's line as written and that only the architect can decide whether the root spec changes; the completion summary reports it. Not recorded as a departure: the child's own spec is empty, so there is no design of this issue to depart from.

findings.finding: F7: the merge-side criterion (file on main via a merged pull request) can be read by no phase before the merge, yet the model plan let the reviewer write `none` on Not proven / risk.
findings.answer: Implementer task 4 seeds Not proven / risk with the standing AC7 claim; the reviewer keeps it word for word and `none` is never valid before the production check; AC7 reads at M (`?ref=<mergeCommit>`), never at `?ref=main`.

findings.finding: F8: a refused handoff_complete (HANDOFF_NO_RUN and kin) needs a stated response.
findings.answer: Tasks preamble: a refused completion is quoted verbatim to the architect; nothing is pushed again and no second handoff is written. (The daemon's record shows this planner was spawned by a run with generation 1 and phase planning, so HANDOFF_NO_RUN is not expected.)

findings.finding: F9: requiredSkills must be filled although the repository ships no domain skill.
findings.answer: requiredSkills lists skill://legion-worker and its references (plus skill://legion-retro for the implementer) with one line each on why, and an explicit `none (repository domain skill)` entry naming the two fixture skills; D9 records it as information for the architect, not a missing surface.

findings.finding: F10: gapAnalysis and planReview must reach the next roles through plan.json.
findings.answer: This record and planReview below; plan.md carries the same decisions in prose.

findings.finding: F11: the model plan credited the root spec with a two-workflow proof bar and a changed-files allowance it does not contain.
findings.answer: Constants source the proof bar to skill://legion-worker/references/pr-body.md and note LEGSMOKE-1021 as the plan's own bar beside the ruleset's merge bar (gate alone); D6 keeps `check` in the proof bar because both workflows run on every push and a red `check` is a repository change worth a stop.

findings.finding: F12: the model plan cited unmeasured pull requests and sibling keys as precedent.
findings.answer: Sources cite only measured precedent: smoke/LEGSMOKE-1070.md on main, pull request #782 (LEGSMOKE-1110) and its marker bytes, the 24 two-line markers read in smoke/, and #767's merge and head check-runs.

findings.finding: F13: pre-state 404s at B and F were not separate measurements at planning since B == F == main@origin.
findings.answer: Constants state B == F == main@origin == 6d843f28 with no pre-Legion commit (so no fixture departure); pre-state fact 1 says the one read at planning covers all three refs and the implementer takes the B and F reads separately.

findings.finding: F14: digests were given without a command and without a git blob sha1.
findings.answer: Constants carry sha256 and blob sha1 for both files, computed with printf | wc -c, sha256sum and git hash-object; AC2 also checks the contents API's own .sha/.size; every phase recomputes before quoting and treats a mismatch as wrong text, not a wrong hash.

findings.finding: F15: AC7's merge-commit file list only behaves that way for a squash; the merge method was not measured.
findings.answer: Measured: the repository allows squash, merge commit and rebase; #767 merged as the one-parent commit 6d843f28. AC7/D7 state the squash assumption, check `parents` = 1, and fall back to compare/<F>...<M> filtered to this issue's paths when it is 2.

findings.finding: F16: the inherited Acceptance's 'only line' bullet contradicts the allowed second line.
findings.answer: AC2/AC3 land both readings in one check: line 1 byte-exact, at most one further line present only under the CHANGES_REQUESTED trigger; AC7 says the production check reads the AC2 bytes or the AC3 bytes accordingly, so merger and production check judge the same thing.
